final3.name: KeyPouch amenity dispenser + keyed refill pouch
final3.case_for: Only candidate with a real consumable lock-in and recurring revenue. Hardware sells at EUR 35 against ~EUR 10-13 landed, and refill contribution is EUR 2-6/L. The analysis puts year-1 per-account contribution after CAC at roughly EUR 140-960 (base ~440-570), all ASSUMPTION. IP is cheap (~EUR 1-1.5k). The validation sprint is cheap (EUR 400-800) and gives a clear go/no-go.
final3.moat: Account-level consumable lock-in via a keyed cap and pouch fitment, plus an EU registered design (EUR 350), a Danish utility model (~EUR 320) and an optional EU trademark. Chair view: the legal moat is thin. The key interface is likely excluded from design protection as must-fit or technical function, Sweden has no utility model, and the red team sees a design-around in 1-3 months (the analysis said 6-12). The durable part is installed base, a distributor or OEM partnership and service, not key geometry. Defensibility cut from 3 to 2.
final3.key_risks: (1) Buyers reject EUR 8-12/L against generic EUR 3-5/L bulk (unverified), and reject the lock-in itself. (2) Meadow KAPSUL, Tork/Essity and Katrin already run cartridge lock-in and janitorial distribution. (3) The PPWR hotel-minis date is probably 2030 and unverified, so there is no 2027 urgency, and it favours any refill system. (4) Founder channel fit is weak: VELUX and Nilfisk contacts are not hotel amenity buyers, and Nilfisk janitorial distributors are the best lever. (5) Capital of EUR 11-14k exceeds the cap, and a SOM of 25-45 accounts is not credible at 10 h/week (the red team says EUR 3-12k revenue). (6) Cosmetics Regulation compliance and filler MOQs apply if the pouches carry product, and several SKUs are needed.
final3.must_validate_before_sourcing: Gate before any tooling or first order: 5 prepaid pilots or 10 LOIs at >= EUR 7/L, ideally with 1-2 janitorial distributors (ex-Nilfisk) willing to carry it. Get an IP attorney opinion on the key interface plus a freedom-to-operate check against Meadow and Tork. Get two filler quotes with MOQ. Test with an off-the-shelf dispenser, a 3D-printed keyed cap and a single hand-soap SKU. Source current evidence on the PPWR hotel-minis date and Meadow pricing (not verified this run). Keep capital under ~EUR 5k by using off-the-shelf dispenser bodies. Kill if buyers will not pay more than EUR 6/L.

final3.name: Nordic FTX Filter Club
final3.case_for: Best recurring-revenue structure, with a B2B installer channel and ~50% margin on EUR 24-39 sets. It is cheap to test with no stock and no lab fee. It is the candidate most likely to produce a real, if modest, side-business, but it does NOT meet the moat bar as submitted.
final3.moat: As submitted, none that qualifies. The ISO 16890 report and RISE P-mark can be bought by any competitor. The frame design must fit OEM housings, so a registered design is narrow. Installer relationships are non-exclusive. The subscription has no lock-in under EU cancellation rules. Both red teams agree on defensibility 1. It reaches 2 only if converted into a contract moat: an exclusive or preferred-supplier deal with one OEM, or a multi-year filter-service agreement with a housing portfolio or service chain.
final3.key_risks: (1) Compatible filters are probably already sold in SE/DK, so the certified premium may be small. (2) OEM warranty messaging (Genvex says only originals keep performance) and OEM trade terms. (3) The founders' ex-VELUX network reaches roofers and window installers, not ventilation service firms. 8-15 installers in year 1 is optimistic and 3-5 is more plausible. (4) Lab cost is unquoted and may be EUR 6-15k across SKUs. (5) Year-1 contribution of EUR 5-12k may not repay the EUR 7-10k outlay, and the D2C first order is break-even to negative after CAC. (6) Seasonality: first revenue is spring 2027. (7) Market sizing is entirely assumption-led.
final3.must_validate_before_sourcing: Zero-spend gates. (a) A sourced scan of existing compatible FTX filters and their prices in SE/DK. (b) Written lab quotes from RISE and one other lab, with a kill above EUR 5k all-in. (c) At least 5 written trial commitments from ventilation service firms (not roofers) at EUR 24 trade. (d) Ideally one OEM or service-chain exclusivity LOI. (e) A waitlist test: pass at 25 sign-ups or 10 pre-orders, under EUR 10 each. The whole test costs ~EUR 300-450. Without an exclusivity element, treat it as a small reseller business, not a brand.

final3.name: Exclusive-artist wooden jigsaw puzzle
final3.case_for: Lowest capital risk of the licence plays: no tooling (laser cut) and a recoupable advance of EUR 1-2.5k. A pre-sale gate under EUR 500 proves or kills demand before the EUR 6-7k order. At EUR 79 contribution is ~EUR 24, and organic artist-audience orders reach +EUR 16-24 per unit. Design-led founders can execute it. It diversifies the shortlist as a consumer art product, but it is weaker than the top two on moat and repeat.
final3.moat: An exclusive artist licence for the puzzle category (target 5+ years, Nordic/EU, first right on new works) plus numbered editions. Chair view: this is a contract moat that blocks only one artist, not the category. A competitor can sign another illustrator within weeks, and the artist can leave at term. It is real only if the artist is a proven EUR 60+ seller whose audience brings its own traffic. Defensibility 2, not 3.
final3.key_risks: (1) The artist's audience may buy EUR 20-40 prints rather than a EUR 79 puzzle, and paid CAC of EUR 25-45 exceeds ~EUR 24 contribution. (2) The artist holds all leverage at renewal. (3) No repeat revenue. (4) Q4 2026 is already gone, so the first real gift season is Q4 2027 and cash and risk are tied up for ~13 months unless pre-sales justify a spring launch. (5) The post-2020 puzzle trend may have normalised, and premium makers like Wentworth and Liberty already exist (unverified). (6) The museum-shop B2B channel is not a founder edge. (7) Shipping and returns costs are likely understated (EUR 10-14 vs 8).
final3.must_validate_before_sourcing: A signed LOI with a named artist (100k+ followers, proven sales of EUR 60+ products) with category exclusivity and co-marketing commitments. A render-based Shopify pre-order page with ~EUR 300 of ads and 2 artist posts: pass at >= 60-80 paid pre-orders (or 150 refundable deposits) at under EUR 20 blended acquisition cost. A EUR 150-300 laser-cut sample for quality. Carrier quotes for fragile ~1 kg SE/DK shipping. Verified SE/DK packaging EPR and timber due-diligence costs. Commit the EUR 8-10k only after the gate.

chair.vs_first_run: Marginally better, not decisively. Structurally, two of the three (N020 and N014) have recurring revenue and B2B channels, N020 has an actual lock-in mechanism, and prices are EUR 35-79 rather than EUR 15-25, so contribution can absorb some CAC. But after red-teaming, defensibility is only 2, 1 and 2, against the first run's 1-2, so the moat gain is one notch at best. N014 is no better than the Trickle-vent refresh kit it resembles. The licence plays (N035 and N034) replace a copyable look with a contract that blocks only one artist and expires. Every number is an ASSUMPTION. The analysts and red teams had no live web evidence (search budget exhausted, hosts blocked, Firecrawl out of credits), and I did not re-verify. Nothing in this ranking is source-backed beyond the retail prices and the SCB figure already cited in the analyses.
chair.honest_overall_assessment: None of these is a genuinely good idea for EUR 5-10k as it stands. The best, KeyPouch, is a plausible but unproven niche B2B play. Its lock-in is legally thin, its true capital is EUR 11-14k, and its buyers are not in the founders' networks. It deserves a EUR 400-800 test, not a EUR 10k bet. The filter idea is the most likely to make some money and the least likely to be defensible. The licence ideas are gated pre-sale experiments, not moats. My recommendation is to run the cheap kill tests on N020 and N014 in parallel (about 6 weeks, under EUR 1.3k combined), and to run N035's pre-sale only if an artist engages. Be prepared to conclude that no candidate clears the bar. The funnel has still not produced what the founders' edges point to: a product sold through building-industry channels (VELUX, installers, housing associations) with a patentable or certified mechanism or a consumable. If all gates fail, the next screen should start from that edge rather than from consumer categories. The full result is saved at /home/user/OMX30-Dashboard/output/rerun/chair.json.

newIdeas.name: KneeWall Pivot Bracket (self-levelling shelf/hook bracket for sloped attic walls)

newIdeas.problem_solved: Standard shelf brackets assume a vertical wall; on sloped walls shelves tilt or a carpenter is needed. One Danish price page shows DKK 500-1,250 to hang two floating shelves in a sloped-wall kitchen (single source, Low confidence).
newIdeas.moat_mechanism: Utility model/design on the locking pivot geometry. DE Gebrauchsmuster EUR 30 online, up to 10 years (DPMA); EU registered design EUR 350 (single-design fee); prior-art search about EUR 500-1,000 (ASSUMPTION). Honest limit: a copycat can design around a tooth-and-pivot claim in 6 months and a registered design only stops look-alikes; novelty must be checked first. Defensibility 3 at best.

No search-volume data available (Firecrawl/Ahrefs unavailable); Amazon not checked, so absence of a pivot bracket is unverified.

newIdeas.target_customer: Owners of air-to-air heat pumps in SE/DK, HVAC installers, BRFs with shared units.
newIdeas.problem_solved: Coarse filters are washed, but air-purification/pollen filters should be replaced yearly; owners are unsure what fits.
newIdeas.moat_mechanism: Weakest of the set: installer reseller relationships plus a model-fit database and a lab test report; no patent. Defensibility about 2. Pursue only if installers confirm demand.
newIdeas.trend_evidence: BRF maintenance sheets and installer guides: clean filters regularly, replace air-purification filters yearly (after pollen season), professional service every 2-3 years. No third-party insert pricing found (Low confidence).
newIdeas.channel_edge: Installer network; low CAC if resold as a service add-on.

newIdeas.name: Homecare Move-In Box (annual-refill care subscription for new owners)
newIdeas.concept: Welcome box for new apartment/house owners bundling the ventilation filter set, window-seal service kit, hygrometer card and dated maintenance calendar, with a yearly refill box on subscription. Bought by estate agents, BRFs and developers as closing gifts.
newIdeas.target_customer: Estate agents, new-build developers, BRFs, landlords (B2B gifting); new owners (B2C).
newIdeas.problem_solved: New owners do not know annual home-maintenance routines; agents want a useful closing gift.
newIdeas.moat_mechanism: Bundle of the certified filter SKUs plus the seal kit, B2B gifting contracts and recurring refill; a copycat must replicate the certified SKUs and the channel. Honest: depends on the other SKUs working, defensibility about 2-3. Estate-agent gifting demand is an unverified ASSUMPTION.
newIdeas.trend_evidence: Built on the verified annual maintenance schedules (filters, gaskets). No direct evidence for agent gifting; validate with about 5 calls.
newIdeas.channel_edge: Founder network in construction and housing; developers and BRFs; Shopify subscription.

newIdeas.name: Hood Filter Pack (grease and carbon filters for popular Nordic cooker hoods)
newIdeas.concept: Model-matched washable grease filters and carbon filters in annual packs sold via kitchen renovators and installers, with carbon filters on subscription.
newIdeas.target_customer: Households with recirculating hoods; kitchen installers; property managers.
newIdeas.problem_solved: Model-specific carbon filters are hard to find and priced as OEM spares.

newIdeas.trend_evidence: Bauhaus lists Thermex carbon filters for specific hoods (OEM spare category exists); no price or volume checked (Low confidence).
newIdeas.channel_edge: Installers and kitchen renovators.

newIdeas.name: KeyPouch: keyed bulk-amenity dispenser + proprietary refill pouch for small hotels, hostels, B&Bs and STR operators
newIdeas.concept: Wall-mounted lockable single/double chamber dispenser (off-the-shelf ABS body, own-design keyed cap/fitment) fed by 1 L stand-up refill pouches with a matching keyed spout. Pouches (shampoo, shower gel, hand soap) filled by a contract filler or sold empty with fitment. Sold first to small hotels/hostels/B&Bs/STR operators ahead of the EU single-use miniature toiletry ban; consumer bathroom refill spin-off later.
newIdeas.target_customer: Independent small hotels, hostels, B&Bs and multi-unit STR operators in SE/DK (5-60 rooms); property managers with serviced apartments.
newIdeas.problem_solved: Single-use miniature toiletries in accommodation are being banned under the EU packaging regulation; small operators need a cheap, compliant, theft-resistant bulk system without large-chain minimum orders.
newIdeas.moat_mechanism: (1) Consumable lock-in: pouch spout/cap fitment is our own geometry, so the dispenser only accepts our pouches. (2) EU registered design EUR 350 first design (sources conflict on extras: EUR 125 vs 175) plus Danish utility model (brugsmodel) application DKK 2,400 (~EUR 320, ASSUMPTION rate) for the keyed fitment, Denmark only; Sweden has no utility model. (3) Honest limits: Meadow (Swedish) already sells a wall-mounted cartridge system (KAPSUL SleeveLock) and locking dispensers exist; a copycat could clone the fitment in 6-12 months unless design/utility model is enforced. Defensibility ~3.
newIdeas.trend_evidence: Coverage reports EU PPWR Art. 25/Annex V bans single-use miniature shampoo/gel/lotion in accommodation from 1 Jan 2030 (some outlets say phased from Aug 2026; sources conflict, check Regulation (EU) 2025/40). Sources name wall-fixed dispensers or returnable refillables as compliant route. US locking wall dispensers list ~USD 28-35 (10 oz) and ~USD 132 (30 oz 3-chamber), directional only. NOT verified: Nordic small-operator adoption, Visita/Horesta position, pouch-system pricing. euroweeklynews.com was not fetchable.
newIdeas.price_point_eur: B2B EUR 29-39 per single-chamber dispenser; EUR 8-12 per 1 L pouch (ASSUMPTION, Low); consumer spin-off kit EUR 39-49.
newIdeas.est_landed_cost_eur: Dispenser ~EUR 7-10 (ASSUMPTION, Medium-Low); pouch with fitment ~EUR 0.9-1.3 empty, ~EUR 3.5-5 filled (ASSUMPTION, Low).
newIdeas.one_off_tooling_eur: ~EUR 3,500-4,500 single-cavity mould for keyed cap/fitment (ASSUMPTION, Medium-Low; get 3 quotes; >5k is a kill). Pouch plates EUR 300-600.
newIdeas.channel_edge: Direct B2B to independent hotels/hostels/STR operators and property managers using founders' commercial/negotiation skills and building-industry networks; free room-count compliance sheet + sample unit keeps CAC low. NOT verified: that founders hold hospitality relationships.

newIdeas.name: Fire-tested clip-on bunk privacy pod for hostels and group-rental cabins
newIdeas.concept: Tool-free clip-on curtain/panel set for standard dorm bunks (tube-rail clamp frame, removable flame-retardant curtain, phone/glasses pocket, optional blackout). Fabric from a mill with an existing flame-retardance certificate (EN 13773-type test or equivalent, to confirm). Consumer spin-off for kids' bunks/dorms.
newIdeas.target_customer: Hostels, group-accommodation cabins, school/camp dormitories, STR hosts with bunk rooms in SE/DK.
newIdeas.problem_solved: Hostel guests want privacy and darkness; consumer bunk curtains carry no fire rating while contract curtains must be certified in various countries, so owners skip curtains or buy non-compliant ones.
newIdeas.moat_mechanism: Modest, ~2-3: (1) independent flame test certificate on the finished assembly (est. EUR 600-1,200, ASSUMPTION, Low), which rivals must also pay for to sell contract, though mills already sell pre-certified fabric; (2) EU registered design for the clamp frame EUR 350; (3) multi-bed hostel pricing and compliance paperwork. A copycat can buy certified fabric and a generic frame within months; real barrier is the certificate on the assembly and hostel buyer listings.
newIdeas.trend_evidence: Marketplace bunk curtains are sold on light-blocking/breathability with no fire rating (Fruugo). A UK fabric supplier states certification to fire-retardant standards is legally required in contract curtain environments in various countries and domestic fabrics are normally not flame retardant (cites EN 13773). NOT verified: Swedish/Danish hostel fire rules, hostel counts, competitor contract products or prices.
newIdeas.price_point_eur: B2B EUR 49-65 per bunk set; consumer EUR 59-79 (ASSUMPTION, Low).
newIdeas.est_landed_cost_eur: ~EUR 18-26 per set incl. frame and certified fabric (ASSUMPTION, Low-Medium).
newIdeas.one_off_tooling_eur: ~EUR 500-1,500 bend/clamp jig for steel tube frame (ASSUMPTION, Low-Medium); no injection mould.
newIdeas.channel_edge: Quote-per-bed offers direct to hostel/cabin operators; founders' sourcing/negotiation for certified fabric. NOT verified: founders' hostel-owner relationships.

newIdeas.name: Kommun-matched kitchen sorting station for BRF/andelsforeninger (pictogram label set + modular cabinet-door rack)
newIdeas.concept: Modular under-sink/cabinet-door sorting rack (bent powder-coated steel, 2-4 slim bins) delivered with printed pictogram labels matched to the resident's municipality fractions (Sweden's municipalities differ; Denmark sorts 10 fractions). Bought in bulk by associations as a welcome-pack item when they set up packaging collection.
newIdeas.target_customer: BRFs and housing associations (esp. those starting property-adjacent packaging collection), property managers, new-build developers handing over apartments.
newIdeas.problem_solved: Residents mis-sort because kitchen setup does not match the building's fractions; associations pay for contaminated bins and information campaigns while adding a miljorum.
newIdeas.moat_mechanism: Weak-moderate, ~2-3: (1) per-municipality label/fraction dataset that is tedious to build and keep current (data moat, not a patent); (2) EU registered design on the rack EUR 350; (3) B2B channel via property managers and founders' housing-association relationships (warm but not proven for sorting). A generic rack is easy to copy; the defensible part is the compliance-matched bundle and framework deals.
newIdeas.trend_evidence: Sources state property owners incl. BRFs must offer packaging collection adjacent to the property from 1 Jan 2027, municipalities responsible since 2024; one source reports a deferral, so date is uncertain. Municipal pages tell associations to review food-waste separation and reserve space. NOT verified: any in-apartment bin requirement, BRF counts, competitor rack prices.
newIdeas.price_point_eur: B2B EUR 29-39 per apartment kit; retail EUR 45-59 (ASSUMPTION, Low).
newIdeas.est_landed_cost_eur: ~EUR 11-15 per kit incl. printed labels (ASSUMPTION, Low-Medium).
newIdeas.est_first_order_eur: ~EUR 4,500-6,000 for ~350 kits plus EUR 350 design registration (ASSUMPTION).
newIdeas.channel_edge: Pitch to property managers and boards when planning the miljorum investment; framework deals via founders' negotiation/pricing. Risk: long B2B cycles for a 10 h/week team.

newIdeas.name: Roof-window corner re-seal patch kit (pre-formed butyl/aluminium corner pieces for common flashing/glazing joints)
newIdeas.concept: Kit of die-cut, pre-formed butyl-backed aluminium corner and joint patches for the joints where roof-window seals commonly fail, with primer wipe and laminated instruction card. Sold to roofers/maintenance teams as a quick small-job fix, to homeowners as DIY, and as a dealer pack for roofing wholesalers.
newIdeas.target_customer: Roofers, housing-association maintenance staff, homeowners with older roof windows.
newIdeas.problem_solved: Owners report leaks at roof-window joints and roofers decline small resealing jobs, leaving improvised silicone repairs.
newIdeas.moat_mechanism: Weak, ~2: (1) pre-formed die-cut geometry matched per window family (die ~EUR 500-800) is a mild know-how barrier; (2) EU registered design EUR 350; (3) optional independent water-tightness test (est. EUR 800-1,500, ASSUMPTION, Low) as a marketing asset. A copycat could replicate in months; the case rests on B2B referral channels, not IP.
newIdeas.trend_evidence: Swedish forum threads: leaks around roof windows; one leak traced to glass-frame joint; one poster says three roofers refused a small flashing-joint reseal. NOT verified: search volume, competing flashing-tape/patch products in SE/DK (not searched).
newIdeas.price_point_eur: Retail EUR 34-45 per kit; installer/wholesale EUR 19-24 (ASSUMPTION, Low).
newIdeas.est_first_order_eur: ~EUR 3,000-4,500 for 500 kits (ASSUMPTION), plus optional lab test EUR 800-1,500.
newIdeas.channel_edge: Founders' ex-VELUX knowledge of roof-window geometry and installer/housing-association networks for pilots. Risk: perceived conflict with a former employer's system and any confidentiality limits must be respected.

newIdeas.name: Hospitality bed-leg bug interceptors with plain-language hostel monitoring kit
newIdeas.concept: Passive moulded bed-leg interceptor cups (no biocide, no electronics) for hostel/hotel metal legs and bunk posts, sold in packs with a monitoring card, inspection guide and log sheet in Nordic languages; neutral white/grey colours.
newIdeas.target_customer: Hostels, small hotels, B&Bs, STR hosts, school dormitories; later consumers.
newIdeas.problem_solved: Bed-bug cases are rising in Europe; small operators lack a cheap, passive, non-insecticide early-warning method that looks guest-ready.
newIdeas.moat_mechanism: Weak, ~2: (1) EU registered design EUR 350 protects the look, not the function, which existing interceptors (Climbup, mentioned by the pest-control association) already use; Valpas offers smart electronic bed legs at a different tier; (2) possible third-party trial validation could differentiate but is NOT secured; (3) mostly the bundle and hostel channel. Treat as a fast test, not a durable asset. Avoid biocidal/medical claims.
newIdeas.trend_evidence: A French canine-detection association reported cases up ~50% in June 2025 vs June 2024; BPCA 2025 guidance recommends isolating beds with interceptors on legs; Valpas claims up to 70% fewer incidents (vendor claim). NOT verified: Nordic hostel incidence, interceptor prices, Amazon BSR (amazon.de unreachable).
newIdeas.price_point_eur: Pack of 8 EUR 34-39 retail; B2B bulk EUR 2.2-2.8 per cup (ASSUMPTION, Low).
newIdeas.one_off_tooling_eur: ~EUR 3,000-4,500 family mould (kill risk if quotes exceed EUR 5k) (ASSUMPTION, Medium-Low).
newIdeas.channel_edge: B2B outreach to hostels/STR managers; inspection-guide PDF for low CAC. Weak: no stated founder hospitality relationships and the category is already served on marketplaces.

newIdeas.name: KeyPouch Breakfast: refillable jam/honey/condiment portion dispenser for B&B and hostel buffets (shares the KeyPouch fitment)
newIdeas.concept: Gravity/pump portion dispenser (dishwasher-safe body, same keyed pouch fitment as the amenity system) replacing single-use sachets and portion cups at breakfast buffets and in STR welcome baskets. Operators refill from 1-2 kg keyed pouches; consumer kitchen refill spin-off.
newIdeas.target_customer: B&Bs, hostels with breakfast, small hotel cafes, STR hosts offering welcome breakfasts.
newIdeas.problem_solved: EU packaging rules target single-use condiment sachets in dine-in settings; small operators need a hygienic low-capex alternative that cuts waste.
newIdeas.moat_mechanism: As KeyPouch, ~2-3: proprietary pouch fitment (consumable lock-in), EU registered design EUR 350, Danish utility model option DKK 2,400. Lower than the amenity version because many portion dispensers exist and food-contact compliance adds cost; incremental tooling is small only if built on the shared fitment mould.
newIdeas.trend_evidence: One news item says the EU is banning single-use condiment sachets for dine-in restaurants from August (year and hotel/B&B scope to verify); a German article covers the same theme; Annex V guide lists banned formats. NOT verified: exact legal scope for hotels/B&Bs, Nordic competitors.
newIdeas.price_point_eur: B2B EUR 35-49 per dispenser; pouches EUR 6-9 (ASSUMPTION, Low).
newIdeas.est_landed_cost_eur: ~EUR 9-13 per dispenser incl. food-contact declarations (ASSUMPTION, Low).
newIdeas.est_first_order_eur: ~EUR 3,500-5,000 as phase 2 reusing the amenity fitment (ASSUMPTION).
newIdeas.channel_edge: Cross-sell to the same hospitality buyers as KeyPouch; one account visit sells both lines.

newIdeas.name: Stove-side child fireguard, independently tested to BS 8423
newIdeas.concept: Free-standing/wall-fixed 3-panel steel guard for wood stoves in a slim Nordic profile that folds flat, type-tested to BS 8423 (fireguard standard) at a test house; report number printed on product and listing.
newIdeas.target_customer: Families with toddlers/pets and a wood stove in SE/DK homes and cabins; secondary: housing associations and daycare with stoves.
newIdeas.problem_solved: Hot-surface burns from stoves. Swedish forums show persistent demand for child stove guards, and retail guards found carry no stated test standard.
newIdeas.moat_mechanism: Independent BS 8423 test report (est. EUR 1.5-3k, ASSUMPTION, Low confidence) that stock imported guards do not advertise; EU registered design EUR 350 for the fold profile. Honest limit: BS 8423 is a UK standard (no EN equivalent found), so it is a credibility mark not a legal barrier; a copycat can pay the same fee but would also need a different design because of the registered design. Not verified: SE/DK retailer acceptance of BS 8423.

Bauhaus.se sells the Aduro kaminskydd at 1,295 SEK (~EUR 115 at ~11 SEK/EUR, ASSUMPTION rate), so price headroom exists. Testix ran a kaminskydd-for-barn comparison updated March 2026. Could not verify Amazon listing density.

newIdeas.channel_edge: Shopify + Google intent search (kaminskydd barn); stove retailers and chimney-sweep networks; housing-association/daycare B2B via founders' building-industry contacts.

newIdeas.name: Roof-window and tall-window child-safety stopper (EN 13126-5 / EN 16281), 2-pack
newIdeas.concept: Tool-free or screw-on opening limiter for angled roof windows and high-mounted sashes, fixed child-safe opening gap with quick adult release, tested to EN 13126-5 / EN 16281.
newIdeas.target_customer: Parents in attic/loft rooms, plus housing associations and landlords who must provide devices in children's rooms (Boverket: openable windows/balcony doors where small children stay need fall-reduction devices where fall height is 2.0 m or more).
newIdeas.problem_solved: Existing stoppers target side-hung windows; the Boverket rule creates a compliance need for landlords and associations.
newIdeas.moat_mechanism: Certification: EN 13126-5 child-safety tests (89 mm opening limit and 500 N strength per a 2020 TSS test report), or EN 16281 for consumer-fitted devices; every competitor must pay the same test to claim the mark (est. EUR 1.5-3k, ASSUMPTION). Plus EU registered design EUR 350 and a Danish/Swedish utility model option; B2B 10-pack contracts. Honest limit: Habo and ASSA already hold EN 13126-5 for flat windows; the roof-window gap is unverified.

Search found no roof-window-specific stopper at Swedish retailers (not proven). prEN 13126-5 revision in ballot Sept 2026. Danish child-fall rules not found (BR18 text not located).
newIdeas.price_point_eur: 35-45 per 2-pack (competitors ~EUR 12-15 each); B2B 10-pack EUR 12-15 per unit
newIdeas.one_off_tooling_eur: 2,000-3,500 stamping/die-cast tool plus EUR 350 design registration (ASSUMPTION)
newIdeas.channel_edge: Ex-VELUX roof-window knowledge (fit by window model) and installer/housing-association relationships; Shopify + Amazon DE/SE; Danish almene boligselskaber.

newIdeas.name: Retrofit window air vent with tested airflow and sound attenuation (EN 13141-1)
newIdeas.concept: Slim clip-on/screw-on vent for old window frames in 1960-80s flats and houses with self-draught ventilation, supplied with a test report for airflow and sound insulation.

newIdeas.name: Modular outdoor step anti-slip tread with DIN 51130 R-class test
newIdeas.concept: Interlocking recycled-rubber or grit-aluminium treads for entrance steps, sold as 3-5 step packs with printed R-class test certificate and a frost/salt ageing test.

newIdeas.moat_mechanism: Independent ramp slip-class test (DIN 51130 R-class, est. EUR 800-1,500, ASSUMPTION) with frost/salt ageing that cheap imported mats lack; EU registered design EUR 350 for tread pattern/interlock; B2B contracts. Honest: moderate moat, a competitor can pay the same fee.

newIdeas.name: Barefoot-wet slip-class bath/shower mat (DIN 51097 class C)
newIdeas.concept: Shower/bath mat in grippy TPE/silicone carrying a DIN 51097 slip-class result and test report, Nordic design, sized for small Nordic showers.
newIdeas.target_customer: Households with older relatives or children; care homes, housing associations, spas via B2B.

newIdeas.moat_mechanism: Paid DIN 51097 class C report (est. EUR 500-1,200, ASSUMPTION) plus EU registered design for the pad pattern EUR 350. A SATRA article refers to a bath/shower mat slip standard (number not confirmed; page not fetchable). No consumer test of bath mats found. Bolius notes most bathroom tiles become slippery when wet.
newIdeas.channel_edge: Shopify; B2B to care homes and housing associations; Amazon with test report in A+ content.

newIdeas.name: Nordic Sun-Path Instrument: latitude-engraved brass desk object (city editions)
newIdeas.concept: A solid-brass and oak desk object (gnomon plus engraved base) that casts the real winter-solstice, equinox and summer-solstice noon shadow lines for ONE specific Nordic latitude (Malmo, Stockholm, Copenhagen, Aarhus, Gothenburg editions). It doubles as a tiny physical sun-path/daylight teaching model for architects, installers and design-minded homeowners. Small run, numbered, engraved with coordinates.
newIdeas.target_customer: Architects, building-physics people, roof/window installers and housing professionals (gift or desk piece), plus design-conscious Nordic homeowners who feel winter-darkness; gifting buyers at EUR 99.
newIdeas.problem_solved: Nobody sells an attractive, latitude-correct 'how much daylight will I get' object for Nordic latitudes. Cost to obtain: ~EUR 350 registration plus ~EUR 1.5-2.5k fixtures (ASSUMPTION).

Winter-light/wellbeing interest is strong in Denmark (70,000+ registered winter bathers; sauna/wellbeing boom). Could not verify: search volumes, any Nordic competitor; amazon.de unreachable.

newIdeas.one_off_tooling_eur: 1,500-2,500 fixtures/engraving jig + 350 EU registered design (350 verified via law-firm note)
